question: And that's a better performance than a lot of people expected, even considering how far the Nasdaq has fallen. Do you think we can safely make the statement now that the market has bottomed?
answer: I would. I would. I mean, you know, last week was good. We had a good GDP number. The stock market was up. Bonds were down. And M3 growth was up about $42 billion on the week. I mean, that's what was...

question: All right, the story looks good -- how good? If we've bottomed, do we continue to bounce or tread water for awhile?
answer: I think that the market has to be convinced that the growth in the economy is going to pick up. So I think we probably tread water, but we trend up cautiously. I think we're in the middle of that V, where you have the stock market bounces and then the economy bounces three to six months later. So, as we get better data, I think the market will do better. But I wouldn't expect huge rallies like we saw in April. In other words, I wouldn't predict a May being the same as April -- but a nice trend on the upside. The good news -- the most encouraging news is, institutional money market, which is really key, is up 70 percent year-over-year. That's an astonishing figure. I've never seen...

question: OK, if you want to be ahead of that tidal wave of institutional money, where do you invest?
answer: Well, I think, first of all, being a contrarian is painful. So you have to be prepared for that. We still like the basics. We like financial services, especially the brokerage stocks. We think they've been beaten up a lot. They were beaten up early last June before this sell off occurred. So you want to be in those, because they'll get a nice move on the upside. We also think, if you've got a stomach for it, high tech is probably where you want to be -- i.e. the Nasdaq 100. That will have to lead the market out. If you believe the market's going to rally, you've got to believe in high tech.

question: Would you buy the QQQ?
answer: Yes. I mean, we think that that's really a good investment. We think that it's a way to diversify, avoid single- company risks. You know, even a Cisco -- people who thought Cisco, you can buy, buy, buy. So, you know, if you like that sector, but you're not sure what to buy, the QQQs are certainly something that we would look at.

question: Briefly, what's your time horizon in terms of turning a profit? And what's a reasonable profit for investors to expect these days?
answer: I think, from here on in, if you can get a 10 or 15 percent return in the broader S&P;, you should be very, very happy. I don't think, this year, you're going to get astonishingly positive returns much better than last year. I think, in 2002, 2003, you might get those 20 percent returns that we sort of got used to in the past few years.
